\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{भोजनम्} (bhojanam)}{भोजनम् (bhojanam)}]{\sk{भोजनम्} (bhojanam) — a meal, food}

\label{lesson:SA-C160-bhojanam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for sesame, then the Sanskrit for a chickpea.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{भोजनम्}}
\textbf{\sk{भोजनम्}} — \emph{bhojanam} — \textquotedblleft{}a meal, food\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bhojana} comes from the root √bhuj \textquotedblleft{}enjoy, eat\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9630): \textquotedblleft{}eating\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}a meal, food\textquotedblright{}, already in the Rigveda. MW compares √bhuj with Latin \emph{fungor} \textquotedblleft{}perform, enjoy\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{व्यञ्जनम्} (vyañjanam)}{व्यञ्जनम् (vyañjanam)}]{\sk{व्यञ्जनम्} (vyañjanam) — a curry, a side dish}

\label{lesson:SA-C160-vyanjanam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a chickpea, then the Sanskrit for a meal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{व्यञ्जनम्}}
\textbf{\sk{व्यञ्जनम्}} — \emph{vyañjanam} — \textquotedblleft{}a curry, a side dish\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vyañjana} comes from \emph{vi-√añj} \textquotedblleft{}anoint, adorn, make appear\textquotedblright{}, the root √añj \textquotedblleft{}anoint\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12160): \textquotedblleft{}decoration, sign\textquotedblright{}, and in grammar \textquotedblleft{}a consonant\textquotedblright{}. MW also gives \textquotedblleft{}seasoning, sauce, condiment\textquotedblright{}, the sense behind a curry or side dish.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a meal, then the Sanskrit for a curry.

\textbf{\sk{आहारः}} — \emph{āhāraḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}food, diet\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{āhāra} comes from \emph{ā-√hṛ} \textquotedblleft{}bring near, fetch\textquotedblright{}, the root √hṛ \textquotedblleft{}carry\textquotedblright{} with \emph{ā} \textquotedblleft{}toward\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 1544): first \textquotedblleft{}fetching\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}taking food\textquotedblright{}, and so \textquotedblleft{}food, diet\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{अशनम्} (aśanam)}{अशनम् (aśanam)}]{\sk{अशनम्} (aśanam) — eating, a meal}

\label{lesson:SA-C160-asanam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for a curry, then the Sanskrit for food.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{अशनम्}}
\textbf{\sk{अशनम्}} — \emph{aśanam} — \textquotedblleft{}eating, a meal\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{aśana} comes from the root √aś \textquotedblleft{}eat, consume\textquotedblright{} (MW's second √aś; CDIAL 909): \textquotedblleft{}eating, food\textquotedblright{}, already in the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa. It is not the same word as \emph{āsana} \textquotedblleft{}seat\textquotedblright{}, from √ās \textquotedblleft{}sit\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{कलशी} (kalaśī)}{कलशी (kalaśī)}]{\sk{कलशी} (kalaśī) — a small pitcher}

\label{lesson:SA-C160-kalasi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for food, then the Sanskrit for eating.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{कलशी}}
\textbf{\sk{कलशी}} — \emph{kalaśī} — \textquotedblleft{}a small pitcher\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kalaśī} is the feminine of \emph{kalaśa} \textquotedblleft{}a water-pot, a jar\textquotedblright{}, already in the Rigveda (CDIAL 2920). MW compares Latin \emph{calix} \textquotedblleft{}cup\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{kalaśa} lives on as Hindi \emph{kalsā} and \emph{kalsī} \textquotedblleft{}small pot\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2920).
\end{cousinweb}
